other_added_oil.label: added oil
other_added_oil._note: Non-seed added fats only, since 2026-09-15. Seed oils moved to their own 'seed oil' entry so the app can name them - peanut is a legume and palm is a fruit oil (palm has its own entry too), so neither belongs under the seed-oil label.

emulsifier.label: emulsifier
emulsifier._note: Bare 'monoglycerides'/'distilled monoglycerides' were added 2026-09-09 - they appear in ~19 breads and the old terms only matched the 'mono and diglycerides' phrasing, so they were being missed.

dough_conditioner.label: dough conditioner
dough_conditioner._note: Industrial additives that make dough machine-processable and extend softness - a strong marker of factory bread rather than simple baked bread. DATEM alone appears in 20 of 64 breads. Also covers the two additives most associated with industrial bread: azodicarbonamide (banned in the EU/UK) and potassium bromate (banned in several countries, restricted in California) - neither appeared in this store's data, which is worth knowing.

artificial_preservative.label: preservative
artificial_preservative._note: calcium propionate (mold inhibitor, in 18 breads), sorbic acid and the literal word 'preservatives' added 2026-09-09.

petroleum_derived.label: mineral oil
petroleum_derived._note: Petroleum-derived pan-release/coating agent, found in 7 breads. Distinct from food oils, so kept separate from the added-oil category.

thickener_stabilizer.label: thickener/stabilizer
thickener_stabilizer._note: Texture agents. Mild - pectin is fruit-derived and fairly benign - but their presence means the product needed help to look/feel like the real thing, which is a processing signal. Added 2026-09-09 for yogurt (pectin in Stonyfield/Silk, agar in Forager); also correctly catches starches in snack-type products.

protein_concentrate.label: isolated protein
protein_concentrate._note: Protein fractions separated out industrially and added back. Notable because high protein is often read as healthy, but achieving it via concentrates is a processing marker rather than a sign of concentrated real food (Cabot's Greek yogurt vs. Chobani's, which is just cultured milk).

added_dairy_solids.label: added milk solids
added_dairy_solids._note: Milk solids/dry milk added to boost body and protein. Mild - it is still dairy - but it means the texture was engineered rather than achieved by straining.

added_flavoring.label: added flavoring
added_flavoring._note: "Natural flavor" is an industrially-produced flavor compound despite the name - a processing marker in an otherwise-simple ingredient list.

mechanically_separated_meat.label: mechanically separated meat
mechanically_separated_meat._note: Added 2026-09-12 after researching how other food-scoring platforms (Yuka, NOVA) work and checking our own coverage against NOVA's published ultra-processing markers - this one had zero coverage despite being a well-documented, specific signal (associated with hot dogs, nuggets, low-grade deli meat). Verified against real data before adding: 77 products in the catalog contain the literal phrase 'mechanically separated <meat>', confirming it's a real, unambiguous marker, not a false-positive risk.

hydrolyzed_protein.label: hydrolyzed protein
hydrolyzed_protein._note: Added 2026-09-12, same research pass as mechanically_separated_meat. Hydrolyzed protein (soy/corn/beef/wheat) is a flavor-enhancer-adjacent processing marker distinct from protein_concentrate (which is about protein fortification, not flavor) and added_flavoring (which is about 'natural flavor' broadly). 106 real matches found in the catalog before adding, mostly in seasoning packets and processed meat products.

seed_oil.label: seed oil
seed_oil._note: Split out of 'added oil' 2026-09-15 at the user's direction so seed oils can be named and banner-flagged rather than lumped in with all added fat. Severity stays 2, NOT 3: 4,998 products contain a seed oil somewhere, and severity 3 triggers SEVERE_INGREDIENT_CAP, which would pin all 4,998 at 50 - far broader than intended. The 'tank it' case is the 219 products whose FIRST ingredient is a seed oil (a bottle of sunflower oil IS the seed oil); those are handled by SEED_OIL_PRIMARY_CAP in scorer.py instead. Olive, avocado and coconut are deliberately absent - they are fruit/nut oils, not seed oils, and score 80-100 correctly. Sesame IS botanically a seed oil and is included; remove it here if you consider traditionally-pressed sesame a different case.

artificial_sweetener.label: artificial sweetener
artificial_sweetener._why: Audit 2026-10-02: 1,031 products used these and none were flagged, so swapping sugar for sucralose RAISED a score (sucralose packets 83.8, Sprite Zero 59.4). Severity 2 like added sugar.

phosphoric_acid.label: phosphoric acid
phosphoric_acid._why: Variant C 2026-10-02: colas (not other sodas) linked to 3.7-5.4% lower hip bone density in older women, phosphoric acid suspected (Framingham, Tucker et al., AJCN 2006). Severity 1: association, not proof.
